evidence.source_title: Data Center Frontier - Vertiv’s AI Infrastructure Surge

evidence.source_title: Tom's Hardware - Half of planned US data center builds have been delayed or canceled

evidence.source_title: Grid-Supporting Equipment Supply Chains Constrain the Feasible Pace of Power System Expansion

evidence.claim: The candidate chunk classifies Micron as a direct public-market mapping to HBM and DRAM supply tightness, where AI-driven capacity allocation can create pricing spillovers into conventional memory.

The candidate chunk classifies Samsung Electronics as a key global HBM and DRAM supplier and notes cached evidence that Samsung announced mass production and commercial shipment of HBM4 in March 2026.
The candidate chunk classifies SK hynix as one of the most direct global HBM bottleneck mappings, while requiring live validation of HBM share, customer qualification, capex, and pricing.
The candidate chunk classifies TSMC as a central manufacturing bottleneck for leading-edge AI accelerators and advanced packaging capacity.

The candidate chunk classifies NVIDIA as the core demand driver for AI infrastructure and a source of pull-through demand for HBM, advanced packaging, power, and cooling, but notes it is already the most visible node.

memory_update.content: For New Hotspots Layer 3, prioritize candidates with direct exposure to hard-to-expand AI infrastructure chokepoints: advanced packaging/foundry capacity, HBM/DRAM supply, liquid cooling, and data-center power distribution.
Highest follow-up research priority from this chunk: TSM, VRT, MU, 000660.KS, NVDA, ASML, SSNLF.
Next layer should collect primary-source evidence: latest earnings presentations, backlog/order data, capex plans, customer qualifications, segment revenue mix, and market-pricing checks.
Visible AI leaders may have lower mispricing potential despite high bottleneck scores; smaller or lower-quality names require stronger falsification plans before priority can be upgraded.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs live validation of CoWoS and advanced-packaging capacity additions, customer allocation, pricing, and whether market expectations already discount peak AI demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Central manufacturing and advanced-packaging node for leading-edge AI accelerators. The chokepoint logic is strong because AI compute demand must pass through leading-edge foundry and packaging capacity, but the setup is already highly visible.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs stronger primary-source validation from company orders, backlog, book-to-bill, liquid-cooling revenue mix, capacity expansion, and customer concentration.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Most direct public-market mapping in this chunk to the physical AI data-center bottleneck: high-density power distribution, liquid cooling, thermal management, and deployment infrastructure. Fits the Layer 2 thesis that electrical and cooling constraints can become as important as compute availability.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs updated evidence on HBM customer qualification, mix shift, pricing, bit supply growth, capex discipline, and whether conventional DRAM pricing is benefiting from HBM-related wafer allocation.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Direct public-market mapping to HBM and DRAM tightness. AI-driven HBM capacity allocation can create broader memory-cycle spillovers, making this a clear chokepoint candidate with measurable pricing and supply indicators.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs current primary-source confirmation of HBM market share, HBM3E/HBM4 qualification status, customer exposure, capacity expansion timing, and margin sustainability.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: One of the cleanest global mappings to HBM bottlenecks, with high public-market purity to AI memory demand. Research value is high because HBM customer qualification, supply allocation, and pricing are concrete falsifiable variables.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs market-pricing check: whether future data-center revenue, gross margin, networking growth, and next-generation platform ramp are already embedded in expectations.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Core demand driver for the whole AI infrastructure stack and a powerful pull-through source for HBM, advanced packaging, networking, power, and cooling. Ranked below the pure chokepoint nodes because it is already the most visible AI infrastructure exposure.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs updated order intake, backlog, EUV/high-NA timing, customer capex plans, China restrictions, and the share of demand tied specifically to AI-related foundry and memory expansion.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Upstream lithography bottleneck for leading-edge logic and memory expansion. Supplier scarcity is extremely high, but AI linkage is less direct than TSM, HBM suppliers, or data-center infrastructure providers.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs live validation of HBM4 commercial shipments, customer qualification, yield, foundry drag, memory margins, and whether Samsung is gaining or losing share in AI memory.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Major global DRAM and HBM supplier with potential leverage to HBM4, advanced packaging, and memory-cycle tightness. Lower public-market purity because the company also includes broad consumer electronics, foundry, NAND, and other businesses.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs evidence on custom accelerator customer count, program ramps, networking order growth, margin mix, and whether AI upside is offset by non-AI semiconductor or infrastructure software cyclicality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Maps to hyperscaler custom AI silicon and AI networking, both of which can become scale bottlenecks as clusters grow. The research angle is attractive but requires more customer-specific validation.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs validation of accelerator backlog, hyperscaler adoption, software ecosystem progress, HBM allocation, gross margin trajectory, and competitive positioning against NVIDIA and custom silicon.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AI accelerator competitor with potential pull-through into HBM and advanced packaging. Research priority depends on whether customer traction and supply allocation convert into durable revenue and margin share.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs customer-level evidence, AI revenue mix, optical and custom silicon ramp timing, margin contribution, and separation of AI growth from cyclical carrier or enterprise weakness.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Second-order AI infrastructure exposure through custom silicon, optical DSPs, and data-center networking. Important if the bottleneck shifts from compute to data movement.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs updated evidence on advanced-packaging inspection demand, AI-related foundry/memory capex contribution, order growth, and whether the market treats KLA as too broad a semicap exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Process-control and inspection exposure to leading-edge and advanced-packaging yield complexity. The bottleneck case is plausible because yield learning becomes harder as packages and nodes become more complex.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs direct evidence of HBM and advanced-packaging revenue exposure, tool qualification, customer concentration, backlog, and whether growth is structurally AI-driven or cyclical.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Smaller-cap mapping to advanced-packaging metrology and inspection. Higher mispricing potential than larger semicap peers, but current evidence quality is weaker and requires more primary-source confirmation.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs order conversion evidence, AI-specific advanced-packaging exposure, memory capex timing, China revenue sensitivity, and margin impact from product mix.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Broad semicap exposure to foundry, memory, and advanced-packaging capacity additions. Relevant to AI infrastructure, but less pure and less clearly scarce than ASML or the HBM suppliers.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs evidence on HBM-related equipment intensity, DRAM capex recovery, NAND drag, customer spending plans, and whether demand is incremental rather than normal cycle replacement.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Memory and wafer-fab equipment exposure that may benefit from HBM-driven DRAM investment. The AI linkage is credible but indirect and dependent on memory capex cycles.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs careful validation of accounting quality, customer concentration, gross margin sustainability, liquid-cooling differentiation, backlog quality, and working-capital stress.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Direct exposure to AI server integration, rack-scale systems, and liquid-cooling deployment. However, Serenity priority is reduced by lower supplier scarcity, competitive intensity, margin uncertainty, and quality-risk flags in the candidate chunk.

summary: Within this candidate chunk, the highest Serenity research priorities are the companies closest to hard-to-expand AI infrastructure chokepoints: advanced packaging/foundry capacity, data-center power and liquid cooling, and HBM/DRAM supply. Visibility is already high for several names, so mispricing potential is scored lower where the market narrative is mature. Rankings are research-priority rankings only, not buy/sell recommendations.
